children: Ashford Hospitality Trust's revenue fell 19.4% year over year as hotel dispositions outweighed stronger comparable-property rooms revenue; earnings turned positive from a year-earlier loss, supported by $59.3 million in disposition gains and lower operating expenses.
¹ Reported as “Total revenue”. ² Reported as “NET INCOME (LOSS) ATTRIBUTABLE TO COMMON STOCKHOLDERS”. ³ Reported as “Net income (loss) attributable to common stockholders”.
: RevPAR rose to $140.76 from $131.14; occupancy was 72.63% versus 71.78%, and ADR was $193.81 versus $182.70.
: Four hotel properties were sold during the quarter, generating $135.8 million in sale prices before adjustments and buyer credits.
: Total hotel expenses declined 22.3% to $150.2 million, primarily reflecting dispositions; comparable-property direct expenses increased $2.3 million.
: The company reported substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern and said it is pursuing property sales, refinancing and cash-preservation steps.
